developments.headline: PM Siliņa states 'no business as usual' with US at Munich Security Conference
developments.summary: PM Siliņa told POLITICO that Europe must speak 'direct and clear' to the US in resetting transatlantic ties, stating 'I don't think we will be doing business as usual' following Trump's Greenland threats. President Rinkēvičs emphasized need for increased political and economic pressure on Russia, including enhanced sanctions and fighting Russia's shadow fleet.
developments.signal_category_relevance: Shows Latvia publicly acknowledging US policy unpredictability while maintaining commitment to Western alignment - articulating tension without accommodation, consistent with the no-hedging posture described in dossier Section 14.

developments.headline: Saeima condemns IOC decision on Ukrainian athlete disqualification
developments.summary: Parliament condemned IOC's decision to disqualify Ukrainian skeleton athlete Vladislav Heraskevichus for honoring fallen athletes on his helmet. Multiple Latvian officials including PM Siliņa and President Rinkēvičs criticized the decision, with Rinkēvičs stating athletes cannot be silenced for showing 'what modern Russia is.'
developments.signal_category_relevance: Demonstrates continued vocal support for Ukraine across institutional levels, maintaining Latvia's position as one of Ukraine's most consistent supporters within Western frameworks.

alignment_diplomatic.prior_assessment: Latvia continues maximum institutional integration while expanding economic diplomacy to compatible partners. UAE sovereign wealth fund engagement and regional summit participation demonstrate broadening diplomatic outreach within Western-aligned framework, maintaining zero hedging toward alternative powers.
alignment_diplomatic.updated_assessment: Latvia maintains maximum Western institutional integration while openly acknowledging US relationship tensions. Munich Security Conference statements signal Latvia will articulate differences with US policy (Greenland threats) while remaining structurally locked into Western alignment. Continued vocal Ukraine support demonstrates unwavering commitment to anti-Russian consensus within alliance frameworks.

developments.headline: Latvia announces participation in NATO Arctic Sentry mission
developments.summary: Defense Minister Sprūds announced Latvia's participation in NATO's new Arctic Sentry mission following Brussels defense ministers meeting. The mission builds on NATO's Arctic security focus, particularly regarding Trump's Greenland annexation statements. Latvia is clarifying type and extent of involvement with allies.
developments.signal_category_relevance: Represents Latvia's continued integration into expanding NATO mission frameworks beyond its immediate geographic area, demonstrating alliance burden-sharing and commitment to collective defense beyond Baltic-specific concerns.

developments.headline: First Hunter infantry fighting vehicles delivered and anti-tank mine production agreements signed
developments.summary: Defense Minister Sprūds announced receipt of first Hunter infantry fighting vehicles and signing of agreements for anti-tank mine production facility during NATO meetings. These represent implementation of existing procurement programs within Latvia's defense industrial development strategy.
developments.signal_category_relevance: Demonstrates continued execution of defense procurement programs and defense industrial capacity building within the established trajectory toward 31,000 peacetime force strength described in dossier Section 12.

security_defense.prior_assessment: Latvia maintains third-highest defense spending in NATO at 4.91% of GDP while achieving first operational deployment of domestically produced autonomous military systems. Cabinet approved 40 million euro defense industry allocation with additional 30 million planned, indicating continued defense industrial development within established high-spending framework.
security_defense.updated_assessment: Latvia maintains its defense spending trajectory above 4.9% of GDP while expanding NATO mission participation beyond immediate geographic area through Arctic Sentry involvement. Continued procurement execution (Hunter IFVs) and defense industrial development (anti-tank mine facility) demonstrate sustained commitment to force structure expansion within established defense transformation timeline.

developments.headline: Agriculture Minister faces dismissal speculation over wood processing contracts investigation
developments.summary: PM Siliņa indicated she may seek Agriculture Minister Krauze's dismissal following service inspection findings on controversial contracts reducing LVM timber prices for private processors. Investigation found two agreements were added to support recipients list without justification, with unclear documentation preparation. Prosecutor and State Audit Office reviews ongoing.

economic_tech.updated_assessment: Latvia maintains focus on defense industrial development while addressing domestic economic governance through continued anti-corruption investigations. developments.headline: PM Siliņa survives sixth parliamentary no-confidence vote
developments.summary: Parliament rejected opposition calls to dismiss PM Siliņa with 48 MPs voting against dismissal and 39 supporting it. This was the sixth unsuccessful attempt to remove Siliņa from office, initiated by Latvia First over migration policies, Rail Baltica oversight, and economic indicators. Vote required repetition after previous session lacked quorum when opposition withdrew.
developments.signal_category_relevance: Demonstrates continued pattern of routine opposition messaging without genuine regime threat, consistent with Latvia's chronic coalition instability within stable democratic framework described in dossier Section 15. Opposition fragmentation prevents formation of alternative majority.

domestic_regime.prior_assessment: Latvia maintains consolidated democracy with continued routine political opposition activity. Sixth no-confidence motion against PM Siliņa failed with standard result (46 against, lacking quorum), confirming established pattern of opposition messaging without genuine regime threat. Institutional preparations for October 2026 elections continue within stable democratic framework.
domestic_regime.updated_assessment: Latvia maintains consolidated democracy with opposition parties continuing routine no-confidence procedures that consistently fail due to coalition arithmetic. The sixth unsuccessful attempt to remove PM Siliņa confirms the established pattern of surface political volatility within structurally stable democratic institutions, as coalition holds sufficient votes despite internal tensions.

challenges: The economic_tech assessment rests entirely on a single Tier 2 source (apollo.lv) covering a domestic corruption investigation, yet maintains confidence 3. This week's evidence concerns wood processing contract irregularities, not the 'defense industrial development' narrative that persists in the assessment language from prior weeks.

The institutional category assessment contains identical language from multiple prior weeks ('Latvia operates as parliamentary republic maintaining EU compliance standards with presidential constitutional review powers functioning effectively') without evidence of genuine collection effort this week. Movement=none may reflect collection gap rather than analytical finding.

The Munich Security Conference statements by PM Siliņa ('no business as usual' with US) represent potentially significant diplomatic positioning but lack required competing interpretations. These could equally indicate routine alliance management messaging rather than genuine relationship recalibration.

The economic_tech assessment maintains the 'defense industrial development' framing despite this week's evidence being entirely about domestic governance failures (wood processing investigation). The assessment forces current evidence into a prior narrative rather than letting evidence drive analysis.

The security_defense sources (eng.lsm.lv, tvnet.lv) are both Latvian government-adjacent outlets reporting on government announcements, creating single-source dependency disguised as multiple sources. Confidence 3 is too high for government-sourced procurement announcements without independent corroboration.
recommended_adjustments: Acknowledge economic_tech source limitation explicitly and reduce confidence to 2, or expand collection to include independent economic reporting beyond the corruption investigation within 1 week.
Either conduct genuine institutional collection or explicitly state institutional assessment is based on absence of developments rather than maintaining boilerplate language from prior weeks.

Provide competing interpretation for Munich Security Conference statements: routine alliance consultation versus genuine US relationship recalibration, and assess which interpretation better fits the evidence.

Separate economic governance issues (corruption investigations) from strategic economic positioning (defense industrial development) in economic_tech assessments, or provide evidence linking domestic governance to external economic strategy.
Require at least one non-Latvian government source for security_defense developments within 2 weeks, or explicitly acknowledge source base limitation and reduce confidence accordingly.

story_clusters.headline: PM Siliņa survives sixth parliamentary no-confidence vote
story_clusters.summary: Parliament rejected opposition calls to dismiss PM Evika Siliņa on February 12, with 48 MPs voting against dismissal and 39 supporting it. This was the sixth unsuccessful attempt to remove Siliņa from office.

story_clusters.headline: Wood processing contracts investigation sparks ministerial dismissal speculation
story_clusters.summary: PM Siliņa indicated she may seek dismissal of Agriculture Minister Armands Krauze following service inspection into controversial contracts with private wood processors. Government awaits completion of prosecutor and State Audit Office reviews.

story_clusters.headline: Latvian leaders attend Munich Security Conference, address US-Europe relations
story_clusters.summary: PM Siliņa and President Rinkēvičs participated in Munich Security Conference February 13-15. Siliņa stated there would be 'no business as usual' with US under Trump, while Rinkēvičs called for increased pressure on Russia.

story_clusters.headline: Defense Minister Sprūds participates in NATO meetings, announces military cooperation initiatives
story_clusters.summary: Defense Minister Andris Sprūds attended NATO defense ministers meeting in Brussels and announced Latvia's participation in new 'Arctic Sentry' mission. He also signed agreements for anti-tank mine production facility and received first 'Hunter' infantry fighting vehicles.

story_clusters.headline: Latvian government officials attend Winter Olympics in Milan-Cortina
story_clusters.summary: PM Siliņa and President Rinkēvičs attended Winter Olympics events, visiting Latvian athletes and making public appearances. Siliņa was seen trying Olympic ice and attending hockey training sessions.

story_clusters.headline: Former SAB employee sentenced, Latvian citizen convicted of espionage for Russia
story_clusters.summary: Former Constitution Protection Bureau (SAB) employee Aigars Sparāns had his three-year prison sentence upheld for illegal gathering of state secrets. Separately, a Latvian citizen was sentenced to six years for espionage for Russia.

story_clusters.headline: Eurovision 2026: Atvara to represent Latvia with song 'Ēnā'
story_clusters.summary: Singer Atvara won the 'Supernova' competition final on February 14 and will represent Latvia at the 70th Eurovision Song Contest with the song 'Ēnā' (In the Shadow).

story_clusters.headline: Parliament condemns IOC decision to disqualify Ukrainian skeleton athlete
story_clusters.summary: Saeima condemned the International Olympic Committee's decision to disqualify Ukrainian skeleton athlete Vladislav Heraskevichus for honoring fallen athletes. Multiple Latvian officials, including Siliņa and Rinkēvičs, criticized the decision.
